 COMMON ORDER

The petitioners are aggrieved against the proceedings of the third respondent dated 27.12.2018 and 28.12.2018, cancelling the licenses issued under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 to carry on the business of selling sweets and bakery items at No.78, Sitco Near, Thirumalai Thirupathy Nagar,
Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi, Villupuram District and to carry on the business of preparing sweets and bakery items at Srivasavi Sweets and Backery Preparation Centre- 1, No.78, Sitco Near,
Thirumalai Thirupathy Nagar, Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi, Villupuram District  606 202 and Srivasavi Sweets and Backery Preparation Centre-2, No.76/8A, Sitco Near, Thirumalai Srivasavi Sweets And Backery vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 14 March, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100560946/

sentences.text: Consequently, the petitioner seek for a direction to the respondents 1 to 3 to carry on the business at the above said premises.

2.Heard Mr.Singaravelan, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners, Mr.A.Kumar,
learned Additional Advocate General for Mr.E.Balamurugan, learned Special Government Pleader appearing for respondents 1 to 3 and Mr.Su.Srinivasan, learned Standing Counsel appearing for 4th respondent.

3.It is seen that the petitioners were running a sweet cum bakery stall in the name and style of Srivasavi Sweets and Backery at No.78, Sitco Near, Thirumalai Thirupathy Nagar, Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi, Villupuram District and for preparing sweets and bakery items they had two preparation centres both in Thirumalai Thirupathy Nagar, Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi,
Villupuram District at different door numbers.
4.

It is seen that by proceedings dated 21.12.2018, the Commissioner of Kallakurichy Municipality sealed the preparation centres in Thirumalai Thirupathy Nagar, Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi,
Villupuram District at different door numbers on the http://www.judis.nic.in reason that the same was being run without any permission and against the public safety.
The said order was challenged before this Court in W.P.No.34666 of 2018.
The Writ Court by order dated 28.12.2018 dismissed the writ petition.
Challenging the said order, the writ petitioner filed writ appeal in W.A.No.234 of 2019.

The Division Bench of this Court disposed of the writ appeal on 18.02.2019 by observing as follows:
2.Mr.R.Singaravelan, learned senior counsel assisted by Mr.V.S.Jagadeesan, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that as of now, the appellant has complied with all the requirements and has submitted an application before the Commissioner of Kallakurichi Municipality and a copy of which has been filed in the typed set of papers.
3.On perusal of the above
, we find that the appellant submitted an application before the second respondent much earlier and not after the writ petition was disposed of.

Therefore, if according to the appellant they have complied with all the conditions required under various statutes, then it is always open to the appellant to file an application under the relevant statute for license/permission.
http://www.judis.nic.in

4.Accordingly, while holding that there was no error in sealing the appellant's sweet manufacturing unit for non-compliance of various statutory provisions, we dispose of this appeal by giving liberty to the appellant to file appropriate application/s under the relevant statute within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

On receipt of the same, the competent authority of the Municipality shall consider the same and pass orders on merits and in accordance with law within a period of three weeks therefrom, after conducting an inspection of the appellant's sweet manufacturing unit.

4 6.In the meantime, the present impugned orders are passed by the Food Safety and Drug Administration Department through its Designated Officer cancelling the license issued under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 by citing that the petitioners running the disputed preparation centres without obtaining permission from the Pollution Control Board and Municipality etc.

sentences.text: The said orders are put under challenge in these writ petitions.

7.Since the Municipality has already taken action against the petitioners through their proceedings dated 21.12.2018 and that the http://www.judis.nic.in said action was challenged by the petitioners before this Court, which has culminated into passing the above order passed by the Division Bench as stated supra, I am of the view that the petitioner has to first work out his remedy before the competent authorities in getting such permission/ license to run such preparation centres at the disputed sites and only when they succeed in getting those licenses from the competent authorities,
they are entitled to approach the third respondent herein for seeking review of the orders impugned dated 27.12.2018 and 28.12.2018 in these writ petitions.
8.Therefore, these writ petition are disposed of only with an observation that it is open to the petitioner to approach the third respondent for seeking review of the impugned orders dated 27.12.2018 and 28.12.2018, in the event of its success in getting license/permission from the competent authorities for running the said preparation centres at the disputed sites.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
